args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 became unhealthy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following its deploy, with an elevated error rate of 18% and failing health checks. Action taken: performed a production-wide rollback to the most recent healthy release, v2.3.0. Post-rollback verification: all regions now run v2.3.0, health checks pass, and error rate is back to ~0.2%. Next steps: investigate the v2.3.1 changes for the regression before attempting a re-deploy; note v2.3.1-rc was healthy in staging only and did not catch this issue.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

1. **Diagnosed:** `checkout-api` v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
2. **Rolled back:** Deployed **v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was healthy in production — across all regions. Post-rollback verification shows all regions healthy with the error rate down to ~0.2%.
3. **Incident opened:** SEV2 **INC-0001** filed for checkout-api describing the failure and the rollback; the on-call engineer has been paged.

Note: v2.3.1-rc was only ever healthy in staging, so v2.3.0 was the correct rollback target. You may want to investigate what changed in v2.3.1 before re-deploying.
